_comment: Per-callback weakenings of the exact sequence (#19 §5, #44). Callbacks compare more strictly than
anything else in the trace, because they leave no residue in end state: if PSFlow never fires a
handler the DOM is identical and every other section agrees. Order, count and interleaving are all
compared, and an entry here relaxes one axis for one callback.
callback  the handler name, e.g. onNodeMouseMove
kind      count (how many times it fired) or order (where it fired among the others)
ticket    where the difference stays someone's problem, when it is a bug rather than a decision
There is no `arguments` kind, deliberately. An argument that differs has a path, so it is claimed by
a region in regions.json — which records the values and makes someone re-affirm them when they move.
A weakening records nothing, so an argument kind would leave a whole handler's payload unobserved for
as long as the entry survived.
A weakening that forgives nothing fails as stale, and it is judged on what it alone forgives.
Self-consistency ignores this file entirely: a side is held to reproducing its own call log exactly.
Three audit rows in the flow-props-change-after-mount scenario are reachable only because this
comparison is exact (spec #37). If an entry ever appears here, check those first.
Empty until the net captures its first callbacks (#54).
